title: unified-rollouts-enhanced-shadow-canary-rollback-policy
author: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: improve safety and observability of unified rollouts by tightening automated rollback triggers for combined shadow/canary traffic patterns and adding a configurable staging window. This addresses flakiness observed during multi-metric rollouts (see linked tickets) where transient spikes in p95 or model quality cause noisy rollbacks.

Summary:
- Add a configurable staging_window (duration) that delays auto-rollback evaluation for shadow traffic to avoid reacting to short-lived spikes.
- Introduce metric aggregation rules to evaluate multi-metric signals (p95 latency, error_rate, and quality_regression_score) with weighted thresholds.
- Expose new rollout config fields in the API and Console: staging_window_ms, metric_weights, rolling_evaluation_interval, and shadow_traffic_tolerance.
- Update the rollout controller to compute a composite rollback_score and only trigger rollback when score exceeds threshold for two consecutive evaluation windows.
- Add extensive unit and integration tests, and an e2e perf canary that simulates bursty traffic and degraded model variant.

Implementation notes:
- rollout/controller: compute metric windows using the existing rolling window aggregator and add a simple exponential decay to deprioritize old samples.
- rollout/config: new protobuf fields with defaults: staging_window_ms=300000, metric_weights={"p95":0.5,"error_rate":0.3,"quality_regression":0.2}, rollback_threshold=0.7, required_consecutive_failures=2.
- console: UI shows staged evaluation state and historical rollback_score timeseries.
- API: new validation to prevent tight staging_window on production-tier rollout without an opt-in label.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for aggregator logic and composite score calculation.
- Integration tests that spin up a local rollout controller and mock metrics.
- Perf canary (perf-canary) run in staging: shadow a new small-quant model under 10% traffic with synthetic latency spikes.
- Gradual rollout: enable in staging for 48h, then opt-in to production for a subset of customers.

Checklist:
- [x] Define config schema and defaults
- [x] Implement controller evaluation logic and hysteresis
- [x] Add API and Console fields + validation
- [x] Add unit/integration tests
- [x] Perf canary and runbook updates
- [x] Docs and release notes

Related: Linear ENG-3124, ENG-2987, PM-411. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3124/enhanced-shadow-canary-rollback for rationale and evaluation curves.

Notes: This change intentionally keeps the default conservative; most teams won't see behavior changes unless they opt into more aggressive thresholds. The goal is to reduce noisy rollbacks while still catching genuine regressions.

review_comments: Maya Patel: Overall looks good. Two items: please add a unit test covering the edge case when there are zero samples in a window, and add a short note in the runbook about how to interpret the composite rollback_score.
Avery Chen (author): Added the zero-samples test and expanded the runbook section in perf-canary/jobs. Also added a defensive check to treat empty windows as score=0.
Diego Alvarez: Can we make the staging_window configurable via flag for the Dedicated product? We should avoid forcing long staging windows for latency-sensitive dedicated deployments.
Avery Chen (author): Exposed the staging_window flag in dedicated config and added validation to ensure it cannot exceed a tenant-specific max without approval.
Samir Rao: CI failed on a flake in console snapshots, reran and green now. Approving once CI is stable.
release_notes: Enhances automated rollout rollback behavior: adds a staging window to reduce noisy rollbacks, calculates a composite rollback_score from multiple metrics (p95 latency, error rate, quality regression), and exposes new rollout config fields for fine-grained control. Disabled by default; opt-in via rollout config.
